payload.title: The FE GraphQL owner identifies a drift by file::op with '(anonymous)' as the fallback name, so two unnamed (or equally named) operations in one file share one key, and the seeder's subject dedupe records only the first.
evidence: scripts/ci/lib/graphql-operations.mjs:86-94 (op falls back to '(anonymous)', key is file::op, no ordinal)
scripts/ci/validate-graphql-operations.mjs:73-77 (baseline keys are held in a Set)
scripts/ci/validate-graphql-operations.mjs:97-99 (NEW and FIXED are decided by key membership)
tools/aria-poc/seed_drift_findings.py:316-320 (a second drift with the same subject is counted as already recorded)
payload.rule_violated: A drift identity must be unique per drift; a key that two drifts can share lets one hide the other in the ratchet and in the finding store.
payload.notes: When two unnamed operations in one file both drift, the owner emits two entries with the same key and the seeder mints one finding from the first, counting the second as already recorded; its messages never reach a finding, and a baselined key would hide a new second drift in the gate. Latent: the baseline ceiling is 0 and a regex scan of the tracked FE tree at the revision finds one file with a colliding key (useBatchTraceability.ts), and both matches there are comment prose that does not parse as GraphQL, so no real pair collides yet. Close condition: Add a per-file ordinal (or a content digest) to the key and to the seeder subject, and add owner and seeder tests with two unnamed drifting operations in one file that expect two keys and two findings. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 5). Verified at origin/main d716541239.
